metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes (gemini's DialogManager registry carries a dozen tool-free blocking dialogs; the cleanest is checkPermissions' out-of-workspace @file read consent, raised BEFORE submitQuery so no model call and no tool call exist); daemon_capability: incapable (gemini's NotificationType enum has exactly ONE member, ToolPermission, and fireNotificationEvent has exactly ONE caller — fireToolNotificationEvent, reached only from resolveConfirmation — so a dialog with no tool call fires NO hook, and nothing is written to the chat JSONL either); driver_capability: ready but moot -> frozen.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable
driver_capability: ready (moot)

Route: frozen. Gemini CLI genuinely blocks on dialogs that name no tool call — several of
them — but not one of them produces a trace on either transport irrlicht has for this
adapter. Both edges the row asserts are unobservable, and the reason is structural rather
than a mishandled signal.

## Agent — yes, and the product has a registry of them

`DialogManager` (packages/cli/src/ui/components/DialogManager.tsx, in the 0.56.0 bundle)
is a single ordered `if` chain over blocking dialog states. Reading it against the row's
four named triggers:

**(1) sandbox / network-access confirmation — EXISTS, but DISQUALIFIED.** Gemini has a
real one: `confirmationDetails.type === "sandbox_expansion"`, titled `Sandbox Expansion
Request`, carrying `additionalPermissions.fileSystem.read/write` and a `network` flag. It
is raised from `ShellToolInvocation.shouldConfirmExecute` (proactive path) and from a
`sandbox_expansion_required` tool error re-entering the scheduler — so an open
`run_shell_command` is always in flight and its result closes the episode. That is
exactly the shape this row's acceptance criteria exclude; it belongs to
`tool-gate-permission-prompt` / `permission-gate-non-mutating-tool`. Not substituted.

**(2) first-use trust prompt — EXISTS, twice.**

- `FolderTrustDialog` / `MultiFolderTrustDialog` (`uiState.isFolderTrustDialogOpen`), the
  documented Trusted Folders feature. Two properties make it a poor recipe target rather
  than a good one: `docs/cli/trusted-folders.md` says the feature is **disabled by
  default**, and it blocks at startup **before** a prompt is ever submitted — irrlicht's
  own gemini-cli driver already auto-answers it (`grep -qiE 'trust|do you trust'` then
  `send-keys Enter`) precisely because it stalls the REPL.
- **The one this cell would actually drive:** the workspace-boundary read consent.
  `checkPermissions(query, config)` parses `@path` at-commands out of the SUBMITTED PROMPT
  TEXT, resolves each against the target dir, and returns any that `validatePathAccess(p,
  "read")` flags and that exist. If the list is non-empty, `handleFinalSubmit` does:

  ```js
  const permissions = await checkPermissions(submittedValue, config);
  if (permissions.length > 0) {
    setPermissionConfirmationRequest({ files: permissions, onComplete: (result) => {
      setPermissionConfirmationRequest(null);
      if (result.allowed) permissions.forEach(p => config.getWorkspaceContext().addReadOnlyPath(p));
      void submitQuery(submittedValue);        // <-- the ONLY call site
    }});
    addInput(submittedValue); return;
  }
  ```

  and `DialogManager` renders a `ConsentPrompt`: *"The following files are outside your
  workspace: … Do you want to allow this read?"* The user has pressed Enter on their
  prompt and the agent does nothing until they answer, yet **`submitQuery` has not run** —
  no model call, no tool call, nothing in flight. It is the row's premise in its purest
  form, and it costs zero tokens to raise.

**(3) server-driven MCP elicitation — ABSENT.** `elicitation/create`, `elicitationId` and
the Elicit* zod schemas appear in the bundle only as vendored `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`
type definitions. There is no `setRequestHandler(ElicitRequestSchema, …)` anywhere and no
`elicitation` entry in any declared client capability. Gemini CLI 0.56.0 does not accept
server-driven elicitations.

**(4) auto-mode / settings review — EXISTS.** `AdminSettingsChangedDialog` renders
*"Admin settings have changed. Please restart the session to apply new settings. Press 'r'
to restart, or 'Ctrl+C' twice to exit."* — no tool, no way forward but answering. Also in
the same chain: `PolicyUpdateDialog`, `ProQuotaDialog` (quota exhausted mid-turn, offering
a fallback model), `OverageMenuDialog`, `EmptyWalletDialog`, `ValidationDialog`,
`LoopDetectionConfirmation`, `IdeIntegrationNudge`, `IdeTrustChangeDialog`,
`BannedAccountDialog`, the extension-update `ConsentPrompt`, and the `confirm_action`
`ConsentPrompt` family (e.g. `/resume save <existing-tag>` -> *"A checkpoint with the tag
X already exists. Do you want to overwrite it?"*, which also costs no model call).

Three of the four triggers present. `agent = yes`, comfortably.

## Daemon — incapable, and the citation is a one-member enum

gemini-cli's hook system can carry a blocked-on-user signal at all: that is exactly what
`Notification` / `notification_type: "ToolPermission"` is, and the 2.26 sibling rests on
it. The question here is whether it can carry a TOOL-FREE one. It cannot, for two reasons
that are each independently sufficient.

**The enum has one member.** In the 0.56.0 bundle:

```js
NotificationType = ((NotificationType2) => {
  NotificationType2["ToolPermission"] = "ToolPermission";
  return NotificationType2;
})(NotificationType || {});
```

and `docs/hooks/reference.md` documents the `Notification` event's `notification_type` as
`("ToolPermission")` — the parenthesised list of one. There is no value a tool-free dialog
could use.

**The producer has one caller.** `fireNotificationEvent(type, message, details)` is called
from exactly one place in the whole bundle: `fireToolNotificationEvent(confirmationDetails)`,
which hard-codes `"ToolPermission"`. That in turn is called from exactly one place:
`notifyHooks(deps, details)` inside `resolveConfirmation` — the tool-confirmation loop,
entered only for a call that already exists in the scheduler. A dialog raised by no tool
call never reaches it. So gemini fires **no hook of any kind** for a class-2 dialog: not a
mis-typed one the adapter drops, not a matcher-filtered one — none.

**The transcript is silent too.** The adapter's Source is
`agent.FilesUnderRoot{Dir: ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/chats/}` over `*.jsonl`. For the
primary trigger, `submitQuery` has not run when the modal paints, so not even the user
message is on disk yet — the session has nothing to move it to `working`, let alone to
`waiting`. For a mid-turn dialog (`ProQuotaDialog`, `LoopDetectionConfirmation`) the
confirmation is live React state; gemini persists tool calls only via
`recordCompletedToolCalls` after resolution, and the parser closes a toolCall the moment
its status is terminal — there is no pending/awaiting record to read.

**And no classifier rung claims it.** Walk `state_classifier.go` while such a dialog is on
screen: `PermissionPending` is hook-only and no hook fired; `TranscriptPermissionPending`
is copilot's signal; `NeedsUserAttention` needs an open `AskUserQuestion`/`ExitPlanMode`;
`OpenToolStalled` needs an open edit/write tool — which this row's premise excludes by
definition; `IdlePromptPending` is claudecode's `Notification/idle_prompt`. Nothing fires.
The session reads `ready` (or `working`, for a mid-turn dialog) for the entire time the
modal blocks the agent, and BOTH edges the row asserts are missing.

## Why `incapable` and not `bug` — the claudecode contrast is the point

The claudecode cell for this same row is `daemon = bug`, and that is the right call there
for a reason that does not transfer: Claude Code DOES emit a signal for its tool-free
dialogs (a `Notification` with `notification_type` defaulting to `permission_prompt`, on a
6000 ms timer), and irrlicht discards it twice over — a matcher pinned to `idle_prompt`
plus a handler guard that drops every other type. The trace exists; the daemon mishandles
it; a PR fixes it. For gemini-cli there is no trace to mishandle. Filing this as a
daemon bug would point the fix at the wrong owner: nothing in irrlicht can be changed to
make a hook that is never fired arrive.

## What would unblock this cell

Either of these, and neither exists at 0.56.0:

1. gemini-cli adds a second `NotificationType` member (or any fire site outside
   `resolveConfirmation`) for a tool-free block. Then this becomes a one-line adapter
   change — widen `handleNotificationHook`'s discriminator — and the row flips to
   `daemon = full` with the recipe below.
2. gemini-cli persists a pending-interaction record into the chat JSONL, giving the parser
   something to read.

Weigh a re-assessment against the retirement date: the adapter is scheduled for
deprecation on 2026-08-20 (PR #1725), so a new upstream notification type is unlikely to
arrive in time to matter.

## Driver

`send`, `keys`, `slash`, `wait_turn`, `sleep`, `start_session` are all implemented by
`replaydata/agents/gemini-cli/driver-interactive.sh`, which is everything the recipe below
would need. Recorded as `ready` for accuracy; it is moot while the daemon axis is
`incapable`, and it is not the reason this cell is frozen.
caveats: THE RE-ASSESSMENT TRAP (this row's version of the vacuous-pass rule): a frozen cell records nothing, so nothing can pass vacuously — but the mirror-image mistake is live. On a future re-check, 'the dialog painted and no waiting appeared' and 'the dialog never painted' produce the identical events.jsonl: nothing. So a re-assessment must carry POSITIVE proof on both sides — a pane capture containing the literal consent text ('Do you want to allow this read?'), AND evidence the hook receiver was actually reachable and logged ZERO Notification lines for that window (not merely that no waiting appeared). Absence of a hook must be observed, never inferred from an absent transition.

THIS HOST CANNOT DRIVE GEMINI AT ALL: the account is tier-ineligible (IneligibleTierError), so no live confirmation was possible and this verdict is a pure source read of the 0.56.0 bundle plus the adapter. Note the honest asymmetry — the primary trigger (checkPermissions' out-of-workspace @file consent) needs NO model call to RAISE the dialog, so the agent-side half of this verdict is cheaply falsifiable even on this host; only the post-answer working -> ready completion needs a model call.

ONE DETAIL NOT RESOLVED FROM THE BUNDLE, MARKED ASSUMED RATHER THAN DISMISSED: checkPermissions gates on `config.validatePathAccess(resolvedPathName, "read")` returning TRUE before it requires consent, which reads as inverted against the method's name. The surrounding control flow is unambiguous (a non-empty list defers submitQuery behind the ConsentPrompt), but the exact predicate that decides WHICH paths qualify was not traced into. A re-assessment driving this trigger should confirm empirically which path shape raises the prompt rather than assuming any absolute path outside the workspace does.

THE TRUST DIALOG IS A WORSE TARGET THAN IT LOOKS, for two reasons that are easy to miss: docs/cli/trusted-folders.md states the feature is DISABLED by default (security.folderTrust.enabled), and irrlicht's own gemini-cli driver already auto-answers it at boot ('accepted trust-folder prompt') because it blocks the REPL. It also fires before any transcript exists, so there is no session row to move to waiting even in principle.

DO NOT LET THIS COLLAPSE INTO 2-19 OR 2-26: gemini's sandbox/network-access confirmation (type 'sandbox_expansion', title 'Sandbox Expansion Request') is real and is genuinely about network egress, but it is raised from ShellToolInvocation.shouldConfirmExecute or from a sandbox_expansion_required tool error — an open run_shell_command carries both edges. Substituting it would satisfy the recipe while testing the row next door.

ADAPTER DEPRECATION: gemini-cli is scheduled for deprecation on 2026-08-20 (PR #1725). Unmaintained is not the same as broken — hook support shipped in #1717 on that same day, and the daemon side of this cell was assessed against the current adapter, not a stale one. The deprecation is a reason to weigh a future re-assessment's cost, not a reason to discount this verdict.

sources.note: THE DECISIVE CITATION. `NotificationType = ((NotificationType2) => { NotificationType2["ToolPermission"] = "ToolPermission"; return NotificationType2; })(NotificationType || {})` — exactly one member. And `fireNotificationEvent(type, message, details)` has exactly one caller in the whole bundle: `fireToolNotificationEvent(confirmationDetails)`, which hard-codes "ToolPermission" and is itself called only from `notifyHooks` inside `resolveConfirmation`. A dialog with no tool call can therefore fire no hook of any kind.

The vendor's own hook reference, section `### Notification`: `notification_type`: (`"ToolPermission"`). Corroborates the enum read from the bundle — the documentation and the shipped code agree there is one value.

DialogManager's ordered if-chain over tool-free blocking dialogs: adminSettingsChanged (AdminSettingsChangedDialog, 'Admin settings have changed. Please restart the session to apply new settings.'), showIdeRestartPrompt, newAgents, proQuotaRequest, validationRequest, overageMenuRequest, emptyWalletRequest, shouldShowIdePrompt, isFolderTrustDialogOpen, isPolicyUpdateDialogOpen, loopDetectionConfirmationRequest, permissionConfirmationRequest ('The following files are outside your workspace: … Do you want to allow this read?'), commandConfirmationRequest, authConsentRequest, confirmUpdateExtensionRequests, accountSuspensionInfo. Same file: handleFinalSubmit's `const permissions = await checkPermissions(submittedValue, config); if (permissions.length > 0) { setPermissionConfirmationRequest({files, onComplete: … void submitQuery(submittedValue) …}); addInput(submittedValue); return; }` — submitQuery's only call site is inside onComplete, so no model call and no tool call exist while the modal blocks. Also the confirm_shell_commands / confirm_action ConsentPrompt handlers, and the keybinding table showing every dialog is answerable with plain keys.

`function checkPermissions(query, config)` — parses @path at-commands out of the submitted prompt text, resolves each against getTargetDir(), and returns those flagged by validatePathAccess(p,'read') that exist. Local, synchronous, no model involvement: the trigger costs zero tokens to raise. Also `saveCommand` ('/resume save <tag>') returning `{type:'confirm_action', prompt:'A checkpoint with the tag X already exists. Do you want to overwrite it?'}` — a second zero-cost tool-free ConsentPrompt.

The Trusted Folders feature is 'disabled by default' and must be enabled via security.folderTrust.enabled; the dialog fires at first run in a folder, before a prompt is submitted. Why the trust gate is a weak recipe target here.

handleNotificationHook returns early on any notification_type != "ToolPermission". Its package comment states ToolPermission is 'today the ONLY member of Gemini's NotificationType enum' — independently re-verified against the 0.56.0 bundle above. installedHookEvents is [Notification, AfterTool, AfterAgent]; all three are tool- or turn-scoped, so none can carry a tool-free dialog.

Source() is agent.FilesUnderRoot over ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/chats/*.jsonl — the only other inbound channel. A ConsentPrompt writes nothing there, and for the primary trigger submitQuery has not run, so not even the user message exists on disk while the modal blocks.

The ladder, walked with nothing delivered: PermissionPending is hook-only; TranscriptPermissionPending is copilot's; NeedsUserAttention needs an open AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode; OpenToolStalled needs an open edit/write tool — which this row's premise excludes by definition; IdlePromptPending is claudecode's. No rung claims a tool-free gemini dialog.

The contrast that justifies incapable over bug: for claudecode the trace EXISTS (Notification, notification_type defaulting to permission_prompt, on a 6000 ms timer) and irrlicht discards it twice (matcher pinned to idle_prompt + a handler guard), so the owner is irrlicht and the route is record-known-failing. gemini emits nothing, so no irrlicht change can make it arrive.

driver_step_types_from_file: exit_clean keys reset_session restart resume send session sigkill slash sleep start_session wait_turn — every primitive the documented recipe would need, hence driver=ready. Also shows the driver already auto-answers the folder-trust prompt at boot, which is why that trigger is unavailable as a recipe target.
The report this row was cut from — the class-1 / class-2 dialog distinction and the finding that only tool-named dialogs reach a subscriber.

recipe.note: Route is frozen on daemon_capability=incapable — no runnable recipe authored. The step sequence is not the obstacle: gemini-cli DOES raise tool-free blocking dialogs and the driver already has every primitive to drive and answer one. Nothing observes it. Documented target for a future re-assessment, in preference order: (1) PRIMARY — the workspace-boundary read consent. Create a file OUTSIDE the launch cwd, then `send` a prompt containing an @-reference to its absolute path; checkPermissions defers submitQuery behind a ConsentPrompt ('The following files are outside your workspace: … Do you want to allow this read?') with no model call and no tool call in flight, answer with `keys`, then `wait_turn` and hold a >=15s trailing idle. Costs zero tokens to raise the dialog. (2) `/resume save <tag>` twice with the same tag — the second raises a confirm_action ConsentPrompt ('A checkpoint with the tag X already exists. Do you want to overwrite it?'), also zero-cost, but a slash command produces no gemini turn at all so the session never enters working and the row's first edge is missing by construction. (3) A mid-turn dialog (ProQuotaDialog on quota exhaustion, LoopDetectionConfirmation) — genuinely tool-free AND mid-turn, so the session really is working when it blocks, but both need a model call and a hard-to-provoke condition. DO NOT substitute the sandbox_expansion confirmation: it is carried by an open run_shell_command and belongs to tool-gate-permission-prompt / permission-gate-non-mutating-tool. Re-author this recipe when gemini-cli grows a second NotificationType member or persists a pending-interaction record into the chat JSONL — and weigh that against the 2026-08-20 adapter deprecation (PR #1725).
